The overall explanation is correct. A main transformer is usually Δ on the generator side and Y on the system side. The Y neutral can be grounded, which helps reduce insulation. The Δ winding lets third-harmonic current circulate inside the delta, which keeps the voltage waveform from distorting. Choice (3) has the two windings reversed, so it is the wrong statement. This matches the official answer.
Reason for (1) is correct: the automatic voltage regulator (AVR) controls terminal voltage through excitation, and the governor controls speed and frequency by adjusting water flow into the turbine.
Reason for (2) is correct: a Kaplan turbine is a propeller turbine with adjustable runner blades, so efficiency drops little at partial load.
Reason for (4) is correct: a Pelton turbine is an impulse turbine driven by a nozzle jet striking the buckets.
Reason for (5) is correct. With N = 120f/p, at a fixed frequency f, a lower speed N means more poles p. Hydro generators run slower than thermal (steam turbine) generators, so they have more poles.
